paper_claim: Language model annotation reliability varies with prompt wording and temperature.
evidence_summary: Methods and Results: gpt-3.5-turbo classified 234 German website texts under ten instructions and two temperatures with ten repetitions each. Agreement across instruction pairs was low (single-output Krippendorff alpha 0.24 to 0.70, mean 0.43), and the two temperatures disagreed (alpha 0.75). Identical inputs also gave different labels; pooling repetitions raised consistency.

paper_claim: LLM performance comparable to trained annotators on legal concepts when guidelines are supplied.
evidence_summary: Sections 5.1 and 6.1: the human annotation guidelines were turned into the GPT-4 prompt, and with them GPT-4 matched the better-performing law student annotators (alpha about 0.51 vs consensus; students below 0.5 scored under 0.4), not the whole student pool. Section 6.5 and Table 3 show predictions are sensitive to prompt formatting; the sample is small (256 sentences, 5 legal phrases) and one model.
